title: Understanding the Cognitive Immersion of Hospitality Architecture in Culture and Nature: Cultural Psychology and Neuroscience Views
research_question: How does hospitality architecture, specifically one that integrates cultural heritage and natural biodiversity, influence human aesthetic experiences and cognitive processes, as understood through the neuroaesthetic aesthetic triad (sensory-motor, knowledge-meaning, and emotion valuation systems)?

participants.description: 3 selected hotel guests (1 undergraduate student majoring in architecture, 1 PhD candidate, 1 tourism blogger from Hong Kong) with different cultural backgrounds, who stayed at Amanfayun hotel in Hangzhou, China.
participants.recruitment: Selected as interviewers/respondents for in-depth interviews after a field survey conducted by a team of six researchers.

stimuli_or_exposures.description: Amanfayun Hotel in Hangzhou, China, an Aman resort designed to integrate cultural heritage and natural biodiversity. Specific features observed include sloping roofs, varied blocks, unified texture/style, mountain views, suites/paths hidden in woods, natural design elements (bonsai, rocky storages), clear structure, easy routes, resemblance to traditional Zhejiang dwellings, indoor suites with environmental control features (modified curtains, retro lamps, hidden modern appliances), proximity to Lingyin Temple and Zhejiang Buddhist College, and yellow earth outer walls echoing local temple buildings.

measures.construct: Aesthetic appreciation and judgment related to architectural design
measures.instrument: In-depth interviews with selected hotel guests, field survey observations by researchers

measures.construct: Sensory-motor responses to architectural features (fluency, complexity, naturalistic patterns)
measures.instrument: Observational assessment during field survey and interview responses

measures.construct: Knowledge and meaning derived from architectural work (familiarity, expectations, context, cultural background)

findings.antecedent: Amanfayun hotel architecture (sloping roofs, varied blocks, unified texture/style)
findings.quote: All the buildings of Amanfayun are unified in texture and style, giving the hotel a harmonious appearance.

findings.antecedent: Amanfayun hotel landscape (mountain view, suites/paths hidden in woods, natural design elements with traditional Chinese aesthetic like bonsai/rocky storages)
findings.mechanism: integration of natural elements and traditional Chinese aesthetics
findings.quote: The suites and paths are hidden in woods... There are also natural design elements that have a traditional Chinese aesthetic...

findings.antecedent: Amanfayun hotel structure (clear, easy route, familiar scene)
findings.mechanism: clear structure and familiar scenes reduce uncertainty
findings.quote: In Figure 2, the structure of the hotel is clear.

findings.antecedent: Amanfayun hotel layout (suites with yards/exclusive access, connected by main road between Buddhist College and Lingyin Temple, similar to traditional Zhejiang dwellings)
findings.mechanism: resemblance to traditional local architecture and integration with cultural landmarks fosters familiarity
findings.quote: Figure 3A shows a corner of Amanfayun that is similar to a typical street scene of traditional dwellings in Zhejiang.

findings.antecedent: Amanfayun indoor suite design (modified curtains, retro lamps/appliances for environmental control, hidden modern appliances)
findings.mechanism: design allows guests to adjust indoor environment, meeting control expectations
findings.quote: To satisfy the expectations of guests about controlling the environment, the indoor suites at Amanfayun were designed to combine elegance and comfort.

findings.antecedent: Amanfayun hotel context (proximity to Lingyin Temple/Zhejiang Buddhist College, architecture/landscape echoing temple buildings, yellow earth outer walls)
findings.consequent: cultural meaning (serenity of Buddhism, cozy feel)
findings.mechanism: architectural design and materials reflect local cultural heritage and context
findings.quote: the architecture and landscape of Amanfayun echo the buildings in the temple and the college... The environment at Amanfayun reflects the serenity of Buddhism in a common way.

findings.mechanism: sensory-motor systems process visual and spatial properties
findings.quote: the evaluation of fluency, complexity, and naturalistic patterns of an architectural masterpiece can be achieved through the sensory-motor systems.

findings.antecedent: environmental features (familiarity, expectations, context, cultural background)
findings.consequent: aesthetic knowledge and meaning of architectural work
findings.mechanism: these factors shape an individual's cognitive framework for interpreting architecture
findings.quote: familiarity, expectations, context, and cultural background directly affect the aesthetic knowledge of an individual and the meaning of architectural work.

findings.antecedent: interaction of sensory-motor and knowledge elements
findings.mechanism: emotion valuation system regulates and balances the interplay between sensory processing and cognitive interpretation
findings.quote: the interaction of sensory-motor and knowledge elements is uniformly moderated by the emotion valuation system, resulting in a balanced appreciation of aesthetic architecture.

findings.mechanism: culture and nature provide restorative experiences that replenish cognitive resources
findings.quote: the study reveals the central roles of culture and nature in cognitive rejuvenation.

mechanisms: Sensory-motor systems process visual and spatial properties (fluency, complexity, naturalistic patterns) to enable architectural evaluation.
Familiarity, expectations, context, and cultural background shape an individual's cognitive framework for interpreting architectural meaning and knowledge.

The emotion valuation system acts as a regulator, balancing feelings and emotions generated by architecture, and moderating the interaction between sensory-motor and knowledge elements for balanced aesthetic appreciation.
Exposure to culture and nature, particularly when integrated into architecture, provides restorative experiences that lead to cognitive rejuvenation.
implementation_implications: Hotel architectural design is critical for consumer hospitality experiences and should consider aesthetic cognitions related to natural sensory properties (color, texture, landscape).
Eco-aesthetics can moderate the relationship between neurorecalibration and longevity, suggesting health benefits.
Hospitality architecture is undergoing a paradigm shift towards integrating cultural and ecological landscapes into structural design.
A neuroaesthetic approach can reveal how the aesthetic dimension of hospitality impacts human cognition, supporting architectural reform informed by neuroscience.

tables.description: Overview of the interview data, including job, gender, age, and domicile of the three participants.

limitations: The study employed a single case research design, which limits the generalizability of the findings to other contexts or architectural styles.
The findings are based on qualitative observations and in-depth interviews, lacking quantitative statistical measures for the reported relationships.

paper_metadata.title: Understanding the Cognitive Immersion of Hospitality Architecture in Culture and Nature: Cultural Psychology and Neuroscience Views
paper_metadata.crossref_title: Understanding the Cognitive Immersion of Hospitality Architecture in Culture and Nature: Cultural Psychology and Neuroscience Views
paper_metadata.crossref_abstract: Hotel architectural design plays a critical role in the hospitality experiences of consumers, and it is important to consider that people may have different aesthetic cognitions toward the sensory properties of nature (i.e., the architecture of the hotel), such as its color and texture, as well as the landscape. While neuroaesthetics has emerged as a nascent field in hospitality research, few studies have investigated how nature reflects aesthetic experiences in the human brain. Moreover, the neuroaesthetic interpretation of architecture through the aesthetic triad is a novel interdisciplinary field. A field survey conducted at Amanfayun, a hotel in Hangzhou, China, in support of our propositions proves that sensory-motor, knowledge-meaning, and emotion valuation systems play key roles in appreciating architectural aesthetics. This study demonstrates that the evaluation of fluency, complexity, and naturalistic patterns of an architectural masterpiece is achieved through the sensory-motor systems. Our results also prove that familiarity, expectations, context, and cultural background directly affect the aesthetic knowledge of an individual and the meaning of architecture. Moreover, the interaction of sensory-motor and knowledge elements is uniformly moderated by the emotion valuation systems, resulting in a balanced appreciation of aesthetic architecture. Finally, the study reveals the central roles of culture and nature in cognitive rejuvenation.
